text:
sara: quick one - sample edge app in examples/edge-onboard is blowing up in the worker: `TypeError: handler is not a function` after our CI bundle step. Works when running locally with node.

devon: error usually means the bundle converted an ESM named export into a CJS default or vice-versa. Which bundler + flags?

sara: tsup (esbuild) using format: 'esm', target: 'es2022', platform: 'browser'. tsconfig currently: ```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "Bundler",
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "allowSyntheticDefaultImports": true
  }
}
```

lee: two layered problem: (A) runtime interop shims from esbuild/tsup, (B) TypeScript overload/generic inference collapse making DX awful.

irene: show the problematic type please.

sara: here's the SDK helper: ```ts
export function predict<T extends object>(opts: { model: string; input: T }): Promise<Result<T>>;
export function predict<T extends string | number>(opts: { model: string; input: T; options?: any }): Promise<Result<T>>;
```

sara: in VSCode inference picks the second overload in a lot of cases and `T` becomes `string | number` which is not what callers expect. When they rely on indexed access types downstream things break.

devon: overload order matters. TS walks overloads top-to-bottom and picks first matching signature for inference. Try reordering or adding a third fallback overload with `T = any` as the most permissive at the end.

lee: For runtime, avoid default exports for worker entry. Worker platforms expect native ESM and can be strict about `exports.default` wrappers. Use `export const handler = ...` and point the worker entry to that named export.

irene: also check `moduleResolution`. "Bundler" is great for most bundlers but can cause different emit than Node's resolver. For edge previews where the platform is Node-compatible, `NodeNext` tends to match runtime ESM semantics better. Add `tsconfig.edge.json` with NodeNext + module ESNext and document why.

devon: esbuild injects `__toESM` helpers when it detects CJS-style imports. Setting `platform: 'neutral'` and `bundle: true` usually prevents introducing the CJS interop if everything is authored as ESM. Also `esbuildOptions: opts => { opts.format = 'esm'; opts.legalComments = 'none' }` helped me.

ci-bot: types:package check failed (examples/edge-onboard): declaration generation error - mismatched overloads.

sara: for the types side I'm considering a small compatibility layer: ship strict internal types under `@redwood/internal` and a developer-friendly facade in the public SDK with relaxed generics: ```ts
export function predict<T = any>(opts: { model: string; input: T }): Promise<Result<T>>;
```

lee: that is pragmatic. Also add a `types/README.md` explaining why we have dual types and linking to DX guidance. Include editor tests: small .vscode/settings.json to run TypeScript plugin completion checks and a CI job that opens a headless VSCode completion snapshot.

irene: add a build sample using Rollup + @rollup/plugin-node-resolve + @rollup/plugin-commonjs so customers who use rollup can see the pattern for worker-only builds.

devon: meta suggestion: update samples checklist in devex repo: 1) tsconfig.edge.json 2) named-only exports for worker entry 3) bundler flags (platform neutral, esm format) 4) fallback public overload 5) VSCode completion smoke test 6) document skipLibCheck rationale.

sara: I'll put up a PR to examples/edge-onboard with: - tsconfig.edge.json - alternate tsup config for edge - swap default export -> named handler - types fallback overload - README + checklist. Will tag @devex and request review.

ci-bot: PR lint: missing changelog entry for sample.

sara: adding one. thanks everyone :rocket:
